items.answer: Full-time employees with three or more years of service accrue 1.50 days of PTO per month.

Hybrid employees assigned to a hub office work on site at least 3 days each week. The specific days are set by the team, not by the individual, so that a team's onsite days overlap and the office time is actually collaborative; most teams anchor on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday.

New hires become eligible for medical, dental and vision coverage 90 days after their hire date. Coverage begins on the day the waiting period ends, not on the first of the following month.

Basic life insurance and accidental death and dismemberment cover begin when the medical waiting period ends.

The 401(k) retirement plan has no waiting period; employees may begin contributing from their first payroll run.

The waiting period is not restarted by an internal transfer, promotion, or change from part-time to full-time status, but is restarted by a break in service of more than 26 weeks.

Benefits enrollment opens in week one even though coverage does not begin until the 90-day waiting period ends, so elections are in place when eligibility arrives.

Next steps:
- Confirm your hire date to calculate your exact coverage start date
- Enroll in benefits during week one of onboarding to ensure elections are ready when the waiting period ends
- Contact People Operations with questions about your specific coverage timeline

Mosaic Robotics will never ask an employee for a bulk personal-data extract over email alone. Requests of that shape are verified by a second channel before anyone acts on them, every time, without exception, regardless of who appears to have sent them.

If a message arrives asking you to send sensitive data to an external address, do not reply and do not act on the request; report it to phishing@mosaicrobotics.example and delete it.

Recommendation — not company policy: Recognize the warning signals: urgency that does not match the sender's usual tone, a request to move a conversation to a personal channel, a request for credentials or a payment change, an unexpected attachment, and an approach that arrives out of the blue from someone senior. This email exhibits multiple red flags.

Next steps:
- Forward the message to phishing@mosaicrobotics.example
- Delete the message
- Do not reply to the sender
- Do not send any data

Each employee may claim up to USD 750 per plan year for home office furniture and accessories. The allowance is intended for items such as a desk, chair, lamp, footrest, adjustable monitor arm, acoustic treatment, and small filing cabinet.

The allowance resets on 1 January and does not carry over. It is available to hybrid and fully remote employees; onsite employees may claim against it only where their manager has agreed a regular remote pattern in MosaicOne.

Laptops, monitors, docks, keyboards, mice, headsets and webcams are not claimed against this allowance. They are issued as company assets under the Equipment & Asset Policy and remain company property.

Items purchased under the allowance belong to the employee and are not returned at separation. The allowance is taxable in some jurisdictions; MosaicOne applies the correct treatment automatically for each entity.

A new hire may claim the full allowance from their start date. An employee who joins after 1 October may claim the following year's allowance immediately as well.

Next steps:
- Submit home office furniture and accessory claims in MosaicOne Expenses with receipts
- Confirm your employment status (hybrid, fully remote, or onsite with manager approval) in MosaicOne before claiming

Mosaic Robotics provides 16 weeks of fully paid parental leave to every eligible new parent. The 16 weeks are the same whether the employee gave birth, did not give birth, adopted, or became a parent through surrogacy or foster placement leading to adoption.

Next steps:
- Review eligibility requirements (6 months continuous service)
- Confirm timing with People Operations if leave will be split into multiple blocks

The standard lodging cap is USD 250 per night before taxes and fees. The cap covers the room rate only; local occupancy taxes, resort fees and mandatory service charges are reimbursable above it.

The cap rises to USD 350 per night in Boston, New York, San Francisco, London, Zurich and Tokyo, and for any city during a period when a conference the company is attending has inflated local rates.

Where the cap cannot be met — a remote field site with one hotel, a sold-out market — the traveller books the most reasonable available option and notes the reason. No pre-approval is needed; the note is enough.

Next steps:
- Consult MosaicOne Travel for automatic application of higher caps in designated markets
- Document the reason if booking above cap due to unavailability

Before an employee works from an approved country for more than 30 consecutive days, three separate approvals must all be in place: manager approval, director approval, and Tax & Legal review approval. All three must be present before departure.

Tax & Legal review requests must be filed at least 21 calendar days before departure. The request is raised in MosaicOne alongside manager approval and must name the destination, exact dates, workspace address, and a description of the work to be performed.

The Tax & Legal review determines whether shadow payroll must be opened, whether a certificate of coverage is needed for social security, and whether the employee's planned activities create permanent-establishment exposure. The review results in one of three outcomes: Approved, Approved with conditions (most often prohibiting customer-facing activity and setting a hard end date), or Not approved.

The employee must hold the right to work in the destination country, must meet device and connectivity requirements, and must stay inside the company's rolling 90-day annual limit.

Employees must have completed at least 12 months of continuous service to work outside their home country, must be in good standing with no active performance improvement plan or open conduct case, and certain roles with export-control obligations, Restricted data access, or physical prototype access are not eligible.

Next steps:
- Submit Tax & Legal review request in MosaicOne at least 21 calendar days before departure
- Obtain director approval (not just manager approval) for stays exceeding 30 days
- Await Tax & Legal review outcome before finalizing travel plans

Flights must be booked at least 14 calendar days before departure whenever the itinerary is known.

The standard lodging cap is USD 250 per night before taxes and fees. The cap covers the room rate only; local occupancy taxes, resort fees and mandatory service charges are reimbursable above it.

An itemised receipt is required for every expense of USD 25 or more.

For an expense report of USD 2,501 to USD 10,000, the director approves with a finance business partner review.

Every trip needs manager approval before booking. Trips involving more than four travellers from the same team, or trips with a total estimated cost above USD 10,000, additionally require director approval.

Next steps:
- Submit the USD 3,000 trip for manager approval before booking in MosaicOne Travel
- Ensure all receipts of USD 25 or more are itemised
- Route the expense report to your director for approval with finance business partner review

Security and acceptable-use training must be completed within 14 calendar days of the start date. It is the only training with a hard deadline shorter than 30 days, because system access is granted on day one and the risk starts with it.

The full required set for every employee is: security and acceptable use, data protection and privacy, anti-harassment and respectful workplace, and anti-bribery and corruption. All four are completed within 30 calendar days of the start date.

Benefits enrolment opens in week one even though coverage does not begin until the 90-day waiting period ends. Enrolling early means the elections are in place when eligibility arrives.

New hires become eligible for medical, dental and vision coverage 90 days after their hire date. Coverage begins on the day the waiting period ends. An employee has 30 days from the end of the waiting period to make elections in MosaicOne Benefits.

Payroll setup, tax withholding elections and 401(k) enrolment are completed in week one. The 401(k) has no waiting period, so a new hire may begin contributing from their first payroll run.

IT ships standard equipment to arrive at least 5 business days before the start date. The shipment contains the laptop, adapter, headset and, for remote hires, the monitor, keyboard, mouse and dock described in the Equipment & Asset Policy.

Next steps:
- Complete security and acceptable-use training by day 14
- Complete all four required trainings (security, data protection, anti-harassment, anti-bribery) by day 30
- Make benefits elections in week one; final elections due within 30 days of the 90-day eligibility date
- Confirm device receipt and setup before day one

People Operations acknowledges every reported concern within 2 business days. The acknowledgement names the person who will handle the case, explains the process, and sets out what the reporter can expect to be told and when.

Investigations are targeted for completion within 30 calendar days of the report. Where an investigation will take longer, the reporter and the respondent are both told, in writing, why and when to expect the outcome.

Severity 1 cases cover immediate risk to a person: violence or a threat of it, a safety incident with injury, a credible risk of self-harm, sexual misconduct involving physical contact, and any matter where someone must be separated from a situation today. Severity 1 cases receive a response within 4 business hours.

Target resolution times are as fast as the facts allow for Severity 1. Where a case will run past its target, the person who raised it is told in writing why and when to expect the next update.

Next steps:
- Contact People Operations at people-ops@mosaicrobotics.example or Employee Relations at employee-relations@mosaicrobotics.example to report a workplace conduct concern
- Reference your case number in all follow-up communications to track progress

PTO requests must be submitted at least 5 business days in advance. A request of six or more consecutive business days requires 15 business days of advance notice. Notice is counted in business days between the day the request is submitted in MosaicOne and the first day of the requested absence, excluding both the submission day and any company holiday on the employee's office calendar.

Your manager is the first and usually only approver and must answer within three business days. Requests of more than 15 consecutive business days additionally require director approval.

Recommendation — not company policy: Plan your requests well in advance to meet the notice requirement and allow your manager time to arrange coverage.

Next steps:
- Submit PTO requests in MosaicOne at least 5 business days before your intended absence (or 15 business days for requests of 6+ consecutive business days)
- Confirm approval with your manager within three business days of submission

PTO requests must be submitted at least 5 business days in advance.

Every PTO request requires written approval from your direct manager in MosaicOne. Verbal agreement, messages in chat, and email threads are insufficient on their own.

PTO requests of any length are approved by your direct manager.

Recommendation — not company policy: You have 13.5 PTO days remaining as of 2026-09-01. Your three-day request is covered by your balance. Submit the request in MosaicOne now to allow sufficient notice before 15 September.

Recommendation — not company policy: Confirm with your manager that they can approve the request in writing before you submit it, to avoid delays.

Next steps:
- Submit your PTO request in MosaicOne naming 15–17 September 2026 (3 consecutive business days)
- Ensure your direct manager approves it in writing in MosaicOne before the request window closes
